ADMIN_PROMPTS.CONTEXT_TITLE: How the AI request is built
ADMIN_PROMPTS.CONTEXT_INTRO: Your instructions are one part of the request. Review the inputs and fixed response format when writing a prompt.
ADMIN_PROMPTS.INPUTS_vision: The food photo, your instructions and an optional description from the user. The language hint is resolved from the user profile; tests use the language selected above.
ADMIN_PROMPTS.INPUTS_text-parse: The user’s food description is inserted through the userText variable. The languageHint variable describes the naming language from the user profile; tests use the selected language. No photo is sent.
ADMIN_PROMPTS.INPUTS_nutrition: A list of products: name, amount and unit. The English name is preferred, with the local name as a fallback. This step receives no photo or recognition coordinates.
ADMIN_PROMPTS.INPUTS_product-label: Photos of one product's packaging and nutrition label, your instructions and an optional user hint. All photos show the same product.
ADMIN_PROMPTS.AUTOMATIC_vision: The code always appends instructions for centerX, centerY and locationConfidence. The user description is added before the prompt when descriptionHint is absent. languageHint is substituted only where its variable appears.
ADMIN_PROMPTS.AUTOMATIC_text-parse: The code always asks for centerX, centerY and locationConfidence to be null because there is no image. Keep userText in the prompt so the description reaches AI.
ADMIN_PROMPTS.AUTOMATIC_nutrition: The products are serialized as {"items":[{"name":"Apple","amount":100,"unit":"g"}]}. They replace itemsJson when present, otherwise they are appended as a separate text part.
ADMIN_PROMPTS.AUTOMATIC_product-label: The code substitutes languageHint and descriptionHint, or appends them when absent. Photos are sent as images. The fixed product_label schema allows null for unreadable fields and does not include food recognition coordinates.
ADMIN_PROMPTS.CONTEXT_EDITING: Use the prompt to describe recognition rules, portion estimates and handling of uncertainty. The code controls field names and types; changing the prompt does not change the response schema.
ADMIN_PROMPTS.RESPONSE_FORMAT_HINT: Read-only format from the actual request builder, sent separately from the prompt with strict: true. required lists mandatory fields; null must be explicitly allowed; additionalProperties: false disallows extra fields. SECOND.TEXT: Nutrition totals come from the foods, recipes and quantities recorded in your account. Check product data and AI estimates before relying on them. The diary makes records available for review; it does not verify every user-entered value.

THIRD.TITLE: Choose what to share
THIRD.TEXT: Your food diary is personal. If you work with a nutrition professional, use an email invitation and choose the categories they can access. Review permissions or disconnect access when your arrangements change.

FOURTH.TITLE: Tools, not treatment
FOURTH.TEXT: Food Diary does not diagnose conditions, prescribe diets or promise weight loss. It does not provide a nutrition professional as part of a subscription. For service questions, account help or data requests, use the contact page.

CONTACT.TITLE: Contact Food Diary
CONTACT.DESCRIPTION: Ask about your account, subscription, a problem in the app or a request concerning your personal data.
CONTACT.NEXT: Write to the support address below. Do not include your password or payment card details.

FIRST.TITLE: Account and access
FIRST.TEXT: Describe what you were trying to do and the message you saw. Include the account email if it is relevant. Password reset is available from the sign-in form.

SECOND.TITLE: Subscriptions and billing
SECOND.TEXT: Include the billing period and a payment or transaction reference if you have one. The Premium section shows subscription status and available management actions. Do not send full card numbers or security codes.

THIRD.TITLE: Report an app problem
THIRD.TEXT: Include the page address, the steps that led to the issue, your browser and device, and what you expected to happen. A screenshot with private details hidden can help reproduce a visual problem.

FOURTH.TITLE: Questions about your data
FOURTH.TEXT: Use the same support address for questions about access, correction or deletion of your data. Describe the request and the account involved. See the privacy policy for information about what the service processes.

DIARY_GUIDE.TITLE: How to keep a food diary you can review
DIARY_GUIDE.DESCRIPTION: A practical guide to recording meals, quantities and notes, correcting entries and reviewing the week in Food Diary.
DIARY_GUIDE.NEXT: Start with one ordinary day. You can add plans, goals and body measurements later.

FIRST.TITLE: 1. Record the meal and date
FIRST.TEXT: Choose the date and meal type, then add the foods or saved recipe you ate. Include snacks and drinks when you want them in the record. For a breakfast with yogurt and granola, add both foods rather than a vague entry called “breakfast”. Separate entries preserve the quantities and nutrition behind the meal.

SECOND.TITLE: 2. Check quantities and units
SECOND.TEXT: Check whether the food data is given per 100 g, per serving or for another base amount. Enter the amount eaten in the matching unit. Half a package is not necessarily one serving: use the label or a measured amount when available. If AI prepared the entry, review food names, portions and nutrient values before applying it.

THIRD.TITLE: 3. Save useful notes and correct mistakes
THIRD.TEXT: A note can preserve a recipe change or a detail you want to discuss later. Save the meal, then reopen it to check the record. If you find the wrong date, food or quantity, edit the entry and review the updated totals. Keep notes factual and useful for you; the diary does not need to be a judgement on the meal.

FOURTH.TITLE: 4. Review several days
FOURTH.TEXT: Use meal history and Statistics to review a period. Check whether repeated meals have consistent quantities and whether missing food data affects totals. A weekly check-in can hold your observations and next steps. If you work with a nutrition professional, share only the categories you want them to review. Records show what was entered; they do not establish a medical conclusion.

RECIPE_GUIDE.TITLE: How to record calories in a homemade meal
RECIPE_GUIDE.DESCRIPTION: Keep ingredients, the finished recipe and the portion eaten consistent. A worked example explains why servings and cooked weight matter.
RECIPE_GUIDE.NEXT: The numbers here are a calculation example, not a recommended meal or calorie target. Check the data for your own ingredients.

FIRST.TITLE: 1. Record the ingredients used
FIRST.TEXT: Use the nutrition data and quantities for the actual ingredients, including oil or sauce that goes into the dish. Check whether each value describes a raw or cooked food. Do not use dry-weight nutrition for a cooked-weight quantity without accounting for the difference. Missing ingredients or incompatible units make the recipe total less useful.

SECOND.TITLE: 2. Check the finished recipe and servings
SECOND.TEXT: Cooking changes the finished weight, particularly when water is absorbed or lost. Keep the recipe’s nutrition basis clear: a complete batch, a serving or a stated weight. Decide how many servings the saved recipe represents and check their nutrition. If the batch changes, review the saved recipe before reusing it.

THIRD.TITLE: 3. A worked portion example
THIRD.TEXT: Suppose a finished dish weighs 600 g and its checked total is 900 kcal, 60 g protein, 20 g fat and 120 g carbs. If the dish is evenly mixed, a 150 g portion is one quarter: 225 kcal, 15 g protein, 5 g fat and 30 g carbs. Water changed the weight, but this example’s total nutrients came from the ingredients. These are illustrative values, not food database values.

FOURTH.TITLE: 4. Save the amount you ate
FOURTH.TEXT: Select the saved recipe in a meal and enter the servings eaten. Check the resulting nutrition before saving. In the example, a recipe saved as four equal servings would be logged as one serving for 150 g. If a serving or recipe definition differs, use that definition instead. Correct a saved entry when the food or amount does not match what you ate.

PRIVACY_POLICY.TITLE: Privacy Policy
PRIVACY_POLICY.CONTENT:
1. General Information

This privacy policy describes how we collect, use, and protect your personal data when using the Food Diary application.

2. Data We Collect

Account data:

  • Email
  • Name, language, theme, and profile settings if provided

Nutrition and health tracking data:

  • Meal records, products, recipes, calories, macro and micronutrients
  • Weight, waist, fasting, hydration, cycle, exercise, goals, and related check-in data
  • Food photos if you upload them

AI feature data:

  • Text descriptions of meals
  • Voice recordings converted to text
  • Food images

Technical, security, and analytics data:

  • IP address and masked IP shown to administrators
  • User-Agent, browser, operating system, and device type
  • Login timestamp and authentication provider
  • Error, performance, and security logs
  • Campaign attribution data such as UTM parameters, landing page, referrer host, anonymous visitor ID, session ID, signup and premium conversion events

3. How We Use Data

We use data for:

  • Providing application functionality
  • Analyzing and improving the service
  • AI features such as food recognition
  • Security and abuse prevention
  • Reviewing successful login history and aggregated device/browser usage in the admin area
  • Understanding which campaigns, referral sources, and landing pages lead to signups or premium conversions

4. AI and Third-Party Services

Our application uses third-party AI services such as OpenAI. When you use AI features, your text, voice, or image data may be transmitted to these services and processed according to their privacy policies and terms.

According to OpenAI documentation, data sent via the API is not used for model training by default, unless a customer explicitly opts in or provider terms change.

5. Legal Basis for Processing

We process your data on the following grounds:

  • Performance of contract for providing the service - Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR
  • Your consent for AI features where required - Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR
  • Legitimate interests for security, service analytics, and campaign attribution - Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR

6. Data Transfers Outside the EU

Your data may be transferred to countries outside the European Economic Area, for example the United States. Such transfers are carried out using Standard Contractual Clauses or other safeguards provided by GDPR.

7. Data Retention

  • Account data - as long as the account exists
  • Nutrition and tracking data - until deleted by the user or account deletion
  • Technical logs - limited time, normally up to 30 days
  • Login activity records - normally up to 180 days unless longer retention is required for security investigation or legal reasons
  • Raw campaign attribution events - normally up to 365 days; aggregated campaign analytics may be retained longer without directly identifying personal data

We do not store raw data sent to AI longer than necessary for processing unless a feature explicitly requires retention.

8. Your Rights

You have the right to request access, correction, deletion, restriction of processing, data portability, and withdrawal of consent where processing is based on consent.

9. Security

We take reasonable technical and organizational measures to protect your data.

10. Policy Changes

We may update this policy. In case of significant changes, we will notify you.
